title: Human-in-the-Loop: Gates That Hold
objective: After this lesson you will be able to place interrupts before irreversible actions, implement approve/edit/skip flows with validated edits, resume exactly post-decision, and audit every human path including skips.
why: Agents that refund, email, or delete without oversight are incidents waiting for traffic. Human-in-the-loop gates risky actions behind people — but gates must be placed, shaped (approve vs edit vs skip), and audited deliberately, or they become rubber stamps (always-approved) or bottlenecks (everything gated). This lesson designs gates people actually operate.

blocks.text: **`interrupt()`** pauses the run with full checkpointed state, surfaces context to a human, and resumes on decision. Placement rule: **before** side effects (refund issued, email sent, account changed) — interrupting after is an autopsy, not a gate. Gate on value and reversibility: money, external messages, deletions get gates; reads, drafts, and internal notes don't (or humans become the bottleneck).

blocks.caption: Gate before the money moves; resume continues with the verdict

blocks.text: Approve, edit, skip: three paths, all first-class

Binary approve/reject wastes human judgment. **Approve** continues unchanged. **Edit** modifies state (fix the amount, soften the draft) — then resumes with *validated* edits (Ch.3 schemas apply to humans too). **Skip** bypasses the action with a logged reason (VIP handled by phone). Design all three paths with tests each; untested paths rot, and rot in gates becomes rubber-stamping or silent skips.

blocks.caption: Fail-closed routing: unknown verdicts skip safely, loudly logged

blocks.text: Rubber stamps and bottlenecks: gate economics

Two gate diseases. **Rubber-stamping**: 100% approval rates mean the gate adds latency without judgment — raise the auto-approve threshold or enrich the review payload (diffs, history, risk flags) until decisions vary. **Bottlenecks**: gating everything queues humans — gate by value × reversibility, auto-approve the rest, and track queue time as a first-class metric. Approval *rate* and *latency* dashboards keep gates honest.

blocks.title: Route the verdicts
blocks.note: Run it: expect 6/6 with zero MISS. Note the last two cases: skip is explicit AND unknown verdicts fail closed to log-skip — gates must be safe under novel inputs, not just tested ones.

items: Interrupt before irreversible actions; gate by value × reversibility, never everything
Three paths (approve/edit/skip), all tested; edits re-validate; unknowns fail closed to logged skips
Watch gate health: approval rates (rubber stamps) and queue latency (bottlenecks) as metrics

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice router and confirm 6/6. (b) Add a fourth human path of your design (e.g. 'escalate-to-lead') with routing + test. (c) Write the gate-placement rule for: sending the reply email, issuing the $500 refund, logging the ticket — which get gates and why, in one line each.
hints: 6/6 baseline first; unknown-verdict case proves fail-closed design, not just happy paths.
Escalate path: decision 'escalate' → 'assign-lead' node; test with a reason field. New paths need tests or they rot.
Email (external, visible): gate. $500 refund (money, irreversible): gate. Logging (internal, reversible): no gate — humans bottleneck otherwise.
exercise.why: Placement (what gets gates), paths (approve/edit/skip/escalate with tests), and economics (bottleneck avoidance) are the three gate judgments — each practiced on concrete cases, not preached abstractly.
exercise.code: // New-path pattern: decision value + terminal/handler node + test + log.

quiz.q: Interrupt placed AFTER the refund-issue node. Verdict?
options: Autopsy, not a gate: irreversible action already executed — interrupts belong before side effects
quiz.explain: Gates prevent; post-action reviews merely record. Placement before irreversibility is the entire point of interrupting.

quiz.q: Approval rate sits at 100% for a month. Diagnosis + fix?
options: Rubber stamp: gate adds latency without judgment — raise auto-threshold or enrich review payload until decisions vary
quiz.explain: Unvarying approvals signal vacuous review. Either the gate is unnecessary (auto-approve the band) or under-instrumented (add diffs/history/risk flags).

quiz.q: Unknown verdict value arrives at the gate router. Correct behavior?
options: Fail closed to logged skip: novel inputs must land safe and loud, never execute by default
quiz.explain: Fail-closed design: unknown → safe terminal + log. Fail-open (execute) turns novel inputs into unauthorized actions.

summary: Gates before irreversibility, three tested paths plus fail-closed unknowns, economics against stamps and bottlenecks. Humans stay in the loop where judgment pays, out where it taxes.
next: Gated actions need instruments: tools with validated args and structured outputs that survive contact with models. Next: tool use done safely.
